title: The continuum function: beth numbers, GCH, and cardinal powers
summary: Reduce infinite function-set sizes to power sets and cofinal powers, and calculate exact values under GCH.
abstract: Taking all subsets of an infinite set produces a larger set, but Cantor’s theorem does not tell us how much larger. The generalized continuum hypothesis specifies the smallest possible increase: each infinite power set has the next larger cardinality. With choice, this hypothesis also determines how many functions there are between any two infinite sets. If the domain is smaller than the target set, the answer turns on cofinality, the shortest length of a sequence approaching the target cardinal from below. This decides whether the function set has the target’s size or the next larger cardinality.
